Subject: Sandbox runbook: LangWeave trace plugin + LlamaIndex connector

Hi Taylor + Ravi —

Thanks again for agreeing to a co-sandbox. Goal: validate the LangWeave tracing shim for token-level spans and the Indexium LlamaIndex connector in a Redwood-hosted dev cluster. We want a lightweight acceptance runbook we can hand to our engineering partners and SREs.

High-level asks:
- Verify trace span schema (see attachment: trace_integration_diagram.png). We expect spans for: request.start, model.call, kv.cache.hit, kv.cache.miss, stream.chunk, and postprocess.score.
- Confirm the LlamaIndex connector handles our KV-cache prefix keys and does not evict pinned entries during workload.
- Run the sample workload (see sandbox_runbook_v1.xlsx) at three loads: smoke (10 rps), nominal (250 rps), and burst (1k rps) and capture p95 latency and token cost.
- Map trace attributes to Redwood telemetry fields: trace_id -> request_id, span.tags.model_variant, span.metrics.token_count.

Acceptance criteria (minimum):
- p95 generation latency < 120ms on dedicated dev instance for the nominal workload with streaming turned off.
- No unhandled exceptions for prefix-cached requests over 5k tokens.
- Trace spans include model_variant and kernel_type tags.

Schedule proposal: runbook validation window next week (Mon–Wed) then a short debrief. Can your teams confirm availability?

I attached a first-pass runbook and a trace diagram. I’ve cc’d Kim and Marissa from Redwood engineering to manage the sandbox infra and the acceptance survey.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partner Programs
Redwood Inference

Thanks Vanessa — this looks great. A couple quick clarifications from LangWeave side:

1) Span naming: we typically emit model.call.start / model.call.end and attach kernel hints as span.attributes.kernel (e.g., kernel=triton_fused). Is it OK if we keep that naming and map on your side to the requested schema?

2) Sampling: by default our SDK samples 10% of streaming chunks to reduce overhead. For the sandbox we can turn sampling off, but wanted to call it out as it will increase noise on longer runs.

3) Auth: we’ll need a short-lived API key for the dev cluster. Can you provision a sandbox key that expires after 7 days?

We are generally available Mon/Tue next week for the run. Ravi and I will align on LlamaIndex connector behavior.

—Taylor

Thanks Kim — quick notes from the Indexium side:

- Connector handles prefix keys by default; we’ll add a flag to explicitly surface cache_hit in the response for the sandbox responses.
- No persistent outbound connections required — our telemetry callback can post traces to the LangWeave ingestion endpoint you provide. We will not pull keys or data.
- For the 5k+ token flows: Indexium will stream back intermediate nodes; please ensure your runtime does not truncate streaming frames. We recommend the test include at least one long-context sample to validate.

We’ll provide a small example serverless function that emits a full-span payload + the trace_id header. ETA Monday EOD: example scripts and expected trace JSON.
